name: NY-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: Valdez's strong fundraising and outside support
Republican candidate with no reported fundraising
Open seat but seat stays with the incumbent's party
model.rationale: The D+25 fundamentals make this a safe Democratic seat, and Claire Valdez has raised $1.7 million with $1.2 million in outside support while the Republican shows no reported fundraising. Markets price a Democratic win at 97%, consistent with the district's lean.
model.watch: A surprise in the June primary or an unexpectedly well-funded challenger could tighten the general, though the district's lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Nydia Velázquez (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Nydia Velázquez's retirement leaves this Brooklyn-Queens seat open, but the district's D+25 partisan lean keeps it firmly in Democratic hands. Claire Valdez enters the general with about $1.7 million raised, $207,000 on hand, and roughly $1.2 million in outside support, with no recorded outside spending against her. Republican Melvin Rivera reports no fundraising figures, and an independent candidate is also on the ballot.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 97 percent, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic margin in the low-to-mid twenty-point range.
